title: Pepsin activity in acidic and neutral protein suspensions
original_forecast: The acid enzyme-containing vessel should show more modelled protein hydrolysis than the neutral enzyme vessel. The acid-only control separates the enzyme state from acidity alone.
original_limitations: Use the reported pH, not the nominal HCl dose. Protein buffering, detailed peptide products and digestive physiology are not represented.

question.original_criterion: Does a digestive enzyme respond to acidity rather than simply to the presence of protein?
question.original_instruction: The acid enzyme-containing vessel should show more modelled protein hydrolysis than the neutral enzyme vessel. The acid-only control separates the enzyme state from acidity alone.
question.assessment: Acid pepsin vessel converts far more retained albumin than neutral pepsin; acid-only blank remains unconverted. Measured pH2.039/6.810 and actual temperature histories replace nominal acidity. Protein buffering, peptide products and physiological or empirical-rate claims remain excluded.
